Not everyone’s built for this path.

Leaving the comfort of a regular 9–5, stepping into uncharted territory, and carrying the weight of purpose on your shoulders—it’s not for the faint-hearted. But I didn’t rebel against the system. I evolved within it.

From early on, people were drawn to something in me. When I worked at Next Retail, I quickly became more than just staff. I wasn’t just folding shirts or checking stock—I became the guy people gravitated toward. Customers would follow my lead, take my advice, and I often found myself walking the floor just speaking to people. My presence sold more than the products did.

That same presence followed me into recruitment—most notably with the British Nursing Association. I became head of recruitment, coordinating shifts for NHS nurses across Kent. But again, it was my energy, not the job title, that made the difference. I was invited into hospitals, met directly with staff, and built genuine relationships. Nurses took on extra shifts simply because I was the one asking. That experience shaped my understanding of connection, loyalty, and service.

But I always knew there was more.

I didn’t leave employment—I evolved into alignment. Today, I work at Distressed Property Group (DPG), a company I’m proud to call home. I’m not a business partner. I don’t own the company. But I run it like it’s mine—because my mentor, who introduced me to this space in 2010, believed in me enough to give me that responsibility.

He trusts me to lead from the front—to manage our clients, oversee our project managers, make strategic decisions, and build this masterpiece we’re co-creating. He’s said it himself: no one outside the legal ownership cares more about this company than I do. And that’s the level of respect I’ve earned—not just as a professional, but as an entrepreneur in the purest sense.

I might be a company man for DPG, but I’m a free thinker. ThinkFree allows me the freedom to express myself fully, and that’s rare. Rare to be able to operate within a structure and still have full creative, strategic and emotional investment in what you’re building.

Everywhere I’ve worked—from retail to recruitment to property—I’ve been seen as one of the best, if not the best. Not because I chased the title, but because I showed up with passion, commitment, and consistency. That’s what entrepreneurship means to me. It’s not always about ownership—it’s about how you show up. It’s about the care you bring into what you do.

And if you truly care about something, you’ll naturally build it like it’s your own.

When you grow up feeling neglected, you either drown or you fight. I fought—but I stumbled many times.

I don’t drink. I avoid junk. I honour rest. I wake up early. I pray. I meditate. I read. I reflect. I grow.

I’m a wounded warrior—but my wounds gave me wisdom. Every scar is a badge of honour. I don’t lead with ego. I lead with experience. I build with love. And I serve with gratitude.

Wealth isn’t just about money. It’s about meaning. And I bring that into every deal, every day.

So wherever you are in your journey—just know this: you're one decision away from changing your entire life. Choose healing. Choose growth. Choose truth.

The best way to find jobs depends on the type of role you’re targeting, the industry, and how proactive you want to be. Here’s a breakdown of the most effective strategies:

	1.	Job Websites (e.g., Indeed, LinkedIn, Glassdoor):
	•	Pros: These platforms aggregate job listings from many companies, making it easier to find a large number of opportunities quickly. Many of these sites also allow you to set up job alerts.
	•	Cons: These platforms tend to attract many applicants, making it harder to stand out. Sometimes applications are filtered by automated systems (ATS).
	2.	Company Websites:
	•	Pros: Applying directly through the company’s website often reduces competition, as fewer candidates might think to go directly. Companies might prioritize applicants who take the initiative to find them.
	•	Cons: It can be time-consuming to visit each company’s site individually. Also, not all companies post their jobs on their own site.
	3.	Reaching Out to Managers/HR Directly:
	•	Pros: This approach can set you apart from other candidates and shows initiative. If you’re able to contact a decision-maker, it may lead to opportunities not yet posted or create a lasting impression.
	•	Cons: Finding the right contacts can be difficult, and cold emailing can sometimes come off as intrusive if not done correctly. There’s also no guarantee they will respond.

Best approach: A combination of these methods usually works best.

	•	Start by applying on major job websites to gain visibility.
	•	Target specific companies you’re interested in by applying directly through their websites.
	•	For positions you’re particularly excited about, find the hiring manager’s or HR’s contact information on LinkedIn or company websites and send a well-crafted email expressing your interest in the role and company.

Networking (through LinkedIn, industry events, or referrals) is also a critical strategy that can increase your chances significantly.

Platform Concept: “Health Tribe” – Personalized Health Coaching & Community Transformation

Concept Overview:

“Health Tribe” is a community-first wellness platform that starts with a personalized coaching program. Users are assessed based on their unique struggles (e.g., lack of time, stress, low motivation, unhealthy eating habits, etc.), and then they are placed into “Tribes”—small, supportive groups of people facing similar challenges.

Each Tribe works together, supporting each other, holding each other accountable, and sharing experiences. The goal is not just individual transformation but also creating a movement where successful users become Health Ambassadors, guiding others on their journey toward a healthier society. The ultimate vision is to turn every user into part of a growing community that spreads wellness, creating ripple effects of health change.

Key Features & Structure:

	1.	Personalized Coaching Assessment:
	•	Users begin with a comprehensive health assessment (via quiz, health history, or even AI-powered chat) that identifies their biggest challenges—whether it’s diet, exercise, lack of time, mental health, or all of the above.
	•	Based on this assessment, they are paired with a dedicated health coach who creates a customized health plan for them, starting with small, manageable steps.
	•	This first phase (around 4 weeks) is all about establishing foundational habits and getting users comfortable with making small, consistent improvements in their lifestyle.
	2.	Tribe Creation – Linking People with Similar Struggles:
	•	After the initial coaching phase, users are grouped into “Tribes” based on their primary struggles and goals. These could be:
	•	Busy Professionals struggling with time management.
	•	New Parents trying to juggle family life and self-care.
	•	Weight Loss Seekers who need support with diet and exercise consistency.
	•	Mental Health Focused who are battling stress, anxiety, or motivation issues.
	•	Each Tribe consists of a small group (8-12 people) and has a dedicated tribe coach to guide them. The members meet in weekly group sessions, facilitated by the coach, but also have daily interactions through the platform’s chat and social features.
	3.	Experience Sharing & Peer Accountability:
	•	Within each Tribe, members share their progress, struggles, tips, and wins. They are encouraged to provide feedback, encouragement, and accountability for one another.
	•	A feature called “Partner Match” pairs people within the Tribe for additional 1-on-1 support—this could be finding a workout buddy, an accountability partner for tracking habits, or someone to share meal planning ideas with.
	•	The community-driven support becomes the central motivating factor, where people are not just focusing on themselves but also helping others—creating a powerful cycle of support and motivation.
	4.	Group Challenges & Achievements:
	•	To keep the Tribes engaged, there are monthly challenges where members compete to achieve health milestones. These could be:
	•	Completing a certain number of workouts as a group.
	•	Sticking to a healthy eating plan for 30 days.

	7.	Hybrid Group & Individual Sessions:
	•	The program would offer a mix of group coaching sessions and individualized support. Each Tribe meets weekly in group settings for motivation, idea-sharing, and team activities, but members also get 1-on-1 check-ins with their coach for more personalized guidance.
	•	Group sessions can include guest experts, interactive workshops (e.g., meal prepping, mindfulness techniques), or even fitness classes that everyone can join virtually.
	8.	Progress Tracking & Data-Driven Adjustments:

	9.	Social Elements & Tribe Messaging:
	•	Each Tribe will have its own private message board or chat room where members can ask questions, share advice, and check in daily.

	10.	Graduation & Long-Term Support:

Not everyone’s built for this path.

Leaving the comfort of a regular 9–5, stepping into uncharted territory, and carrying the weight of purpose on your shoulders—it’s not for the faint-hearted. But I didn’t rebel against the system. I evolved within it.

From early on, people were drawn to something in me. When I worked at Next Retail, I quickly became more than just staff. I wasn’t just folding shirts or checking stock—I became the guy people gravitated toward. Customers would follow my lead, take my advice, and I often found myself walking the floor just speaking to people. My presence sold more than the products did.

That same presence followed me into recruitment—most notably with the British Nursing Association. I became head of recruitment, coordinating shifts for NHS nurses across Kent. But again, it was my energy, not the job title, that made the difference. I was invited into hospitals, met directly with staff, and built genuine relationships. Nurses took on extra shifts simply because I was the one asking. That experience shaped my understanding of connection, loyalty, and service.

But I always knew there was more.

I didn’t leave employment—I evolved into alignment. Today, I work at Distressed Property Group (DPG), a company I’m proud to call home. I’m not a business partner. I don’t own the company. But I run it like it’s mine—because my mentor, who introduced me to this space in 2010, believed in me enough to give me that responsibility.

He trusts me to lead from the front—to manage our clients, oversee our project managers, make strategic decisions, and build this masterpiece we’re co-creating. He’s said it himself: no one outside the legal ownership cares more about this company than I do. And that’s the level of respect I’ve earned—not just as a professional, but as an entrepreneur in the purest sense.

I might be a company man for DPG, but I’m a free thinker. ThinkFree allows me the freedom to express myself fully, and that’s rare. Rare to be able to operate within a structure and still have full creative, strategic and emotional investment in what you’re building.

Everywhere I’ve worked—from retail to recruitment to property—I’ve been seen as one of the best, if not the best. Not because I chased the title, but because I showed up with passion, commitment, and consistency. That’s what entrepreneurship means to me. It’s not always about ownership—it’s about how you show up. It’s about the care you bring into what you do.

And if you truly care about something, you’ll naturally build it like it’s your own.

I’m a wounded warrior—but my wounds gave me wisdom. Every scar is a badge of honour. I don’t lead with ego. I lead with experience. I build with love. And I serve with gratitude.

Wealth isn’t just about money. It’s about meaning. And I bring that into every deal, every day.

The best way to find jobs depends on the type of role you’re targeting, the industry, and how proactive you want to be. Here’s a breakdown of the most effective strategies:

	1.	Job Websites (e.g., Indeed, LinkedIn, Glassdoor):
	•	Pros: These platforms aggregate job listings from many companies, making it easier to find a large number of opportunities quickly. Many of these sites also allow you to set up job alerts.
	•	Cons: These platforms tend to attract many applicants, making it harder to stand out. Sometimes applications are filtered by automated systems (ATS).
	2.	Company Websites:
	•	Pros: Applying directly through the company’s website often reduces competition, as fewer candidates might think to go directly. Companies might prioritize applicants who take the initiative to find them.
	•	Cons: It can be time-consuming to visit each company’s site individually. Also, not all companies post their jobs on their own site.
	3.	Reaching Out to Managers/HR Directly:
	•	Pros: This approach can set you apart from other candidates and shows initiative. If you’re able to contact a decision-maker, it may lead to opportunities not yet posted or create a lasting impression.
	•	Cons: Finding the right contacts can be difficult, and cold emailing can sometimes come off as intrusive if not done correctly. There’s also no guarantee they will respond.

Best approach: A combination of these methods usually works best.

	•	Start by applying on major job websites to gain visibility.
	•	Target specific companies you’re interested in by applying directly through their websites.
	•	For positions you’re particularly excited about, find the hiring manager’s or HR’s contact information on LinkedIn or company websites and send a well-crafted email expressing your interest in the role and company.

Networking (through LinkedIn, industry events, or referrals) is also a critical strategy that can increase your chances significantly.

Platform Concept: “Health Tribe” – Personalized Health Coaching & Community Transformation

Concept Overview:

“Health Tribe” is a community-first wellness platform that starts with a personalized coaching program. Users are assessed based on their unique struggles (e.g., lack of time, stress, low motivation, unhealthy eating habits, etc.), and then they are placed into “Tribes”—small, supportive groups of people facing similar challenges.

Each Tribe works together, supporting each other, holding each other accountable, and sharing experiences. The goal is not just individual transformation but also creating a movement where successful users become Health Ambassadors, guiding others on their journey toward a healthier society. The ultimate vision is to turn every user into part of a growing community that spreads wellness, creating ripple effects of health change.

Key Features & Structure:

	1.	Personalized Coaching Assessment:
	•	Users begin with a comprehensive health assessment (via quiz, health history, or even AI-powered chat) that identifies their biggest challenges—whether it’s diet, exercise, lack of time, mental health, or all of the above.
	•	Based on this assessment, they are paired with a dedicated health coach who creates a customized health plan for them, starting with small, manageable steps.
	•	This first phase (around 4 weeks) is all about establishing foundational habits and getting users comfortable with making small, consistent improvements in their lifestyle.
	2.	Tribe Creation – Linking People with Similar Struggles:
	•	After the initial coaching phase, users are grouped into “Tribes” based on their primary struggles and goals. These could be:
	•	Busy Professionals struggling with time management.
	•	New Parents trying to juggle family life and self-care.
	•	Weight Loss Seekers who need support with diet and exercise consistency.
	•	Mental Health Focused who are battling stress, anxiety, or motivation issues.
	•	Each Tribe consists of a small group (8-12 people) and has a dedicated tribe coach to guide them. The members meet in weekly group sessions, facilitated by the coach, but also have daily interactions through the platform’s chat and social features.
	3.	Experience Sharing & Peer Accountability:
	•	Within each Tribe, members share their progress, struggles, tips, and wins. They are encouraged to provide feedback, encouragement, and accountability for one another.
	•	A feature called “Partner Match” pairs people within the Tribe for additional 1-on-1 support—this could be finding a workout buddy, an accountability partner for tracking habits, or someone to share meal planning ideas with.
	•	The community-driven support becomes the central motivating factor, where people are not just focusing on themselves but also helping others—creating a powerful cycle of support and motivation.
	4.	Group Challenges & Achievements:
	•	To keep the Tribes engaged, there are monthly challenges where members compete to achieve health milestones. These could be:
	•	Completing a certain number of workouts as a group.
	•	Sticking to a healthy eating plan for 30 days.
	•	Mindfulness or stress reduction challenges (like a daily meditation goal).
	•	These challenges foster a team spirit and further drive accountability within the group.
	•	The platform tracks progress, offering group rewards like badges, discounts, or even real-world incentives (e.g., gift cards for wellness products).
	5.	Health Ambassadors Program:
	•	Once members hit certain milestones (e.g., after 3 or 6 months of consistent progress), they have the opportunity to become Health Ambassadors. This is a key part of your vision to build a society of healthy, motivated individuals.
	•	As Ambassadors, they would take on more leadership roles in the platform, helping to mentor newer members, share their journey, and spread the message of wellness. They could run mini-sessions, moderate forums, or simply offer support in larger community spaces.
	•	Health Ambassadors also get exclusive access to advanced wellness tools, products, or higher-level coaching as a reward for their progress and dedication.
	6.	“Tribe to Society” Transformation:
	•	The ultimate goal of the platform is to build a culture of wellness, where each user becomes part of something bigger than just their own health journey. Through the Health Tribe, members are continuously empowered to take charge of their well-being and inspire others to do the same.
	•	Successful Tribes could be recognized in the larger community, creating a society of like-minded wellness warriors. There would be ongoing community events, virtual wellness retreats, and even real-life meet-ups to further reinforce the power of the collective.
	•	Ambassadors who complete their journey could even start their own Tribes, further spreading the message and growing the community of health-conscious individuals.
	7.	Hybrid Group & Individual Sessions:
	•	The program would offer a mix of group coaching sessions and individualized support. Each Tribe meets weekly in group settings for motivation, idea-sharing, and team activities, but members also get 1-on-1 check-ins with their coach for more personalized guidance.
	•	Group sessions can include guest experts, interactive workshops (e.g., meal prepping, mindfulness techniques), or even fitness classes that everyone can join virtually.
	8.	Progress Tracking & Data-Driven Adjustments:
	•	The platform would feature a habit tracker that shows users’ progress on their wellness journey, highlighting streaks, milestones, and improvements.
	•	Based on their progress, the program can adjust goals or provide more tailored advice. For example, if someone is struggling with workouts, they could get tips on easier exercises or suggestions for time management.
	9.	Social Elements & Tribe Messaging:
	•	Each Tribe will have its own private message board or chat room where members can ask questions, share advice, and check in daily.
	•	Users can also connect with people outside their Tribe through a platform-wide forum, allowing for cross-Tribe support and socialization. This is a space for health tips, success stories, and general community encouragement.
	10.	Graduation & Long-Term Support:
	•	Once a user completes a certain number of challenges or demonstrates long-term consistency (e.g., 6 months or more), they “graduate” from the active program but remain part of the Tribe as a Health Ambassador.
	•	They are encouraged to keep participating by helping newer members and staying engaged with advanced challenges or special events.

How This Creates a “Healthy Society”:

	•	The platform is more than just individual success—it’s about creating a network of health ambassadors who actively promote and support health change in their communities.
	•	As people progress and become ambassadors, they inspire others both within the platform and in their real-life circles, creating a ripple effect where wellness habits spread naturally.
	•	Eventually, the goal is to create a self-sustaining society of motivated individuals who actively help each other grow healthier, stronger, and more motivated over time.

Unique Selling Points (USPs):

	1.	Community-First Approach: The focus on Tribes and peer support sets this platform apart from solo coaching apps. The feeling of belonging and being part of a movement is a powerful motivator.
	2.	Health Ambassadors: Turning users into role models and leaders who inspire others creates a sustainable cycle of growth and engagement.
	3.	Tailored Tribes: Grouping people based on their specific challenges and making the journey shared ensures that the advice, support, and accountability are relevant and personal.
	4.	Graduated Support: Users transition from being participants to leaders, ensuring they never feel like they’ve “finished” their journey but can continue growing and helping others.
	5.	Real-World Impact: The program is structured not just for individual improvement but to build a healthier society as users spread their habits and inspire those around them.

Marketing Hooks:

	•	“Join a Tribe, Transform Your Life. Together.”
	•	“Find Your Tribe. Conquer Your Challenges. Become a Health Ambassador.”
	•	“Change Starts With You—But It Grows With Your Tribe.”

This concept delivers a truly community-driven approach to wellness, where people motivate each other and create long-lasting change as a group, all while being supported by personalized coaching. It can inspire a deep sense of belonging, accountability, and personal transformation, making it a powerful and unique health platform.

Not everyone’s built for this path.

Leaving the comfort of a regular 9–5, stepping into uncharted territory, and carrying the weight of purpose on your shoulders—it’s not for the faint-hearted. But I didn’t rebel against the system. I evolved within it.

From early on, people were drawn to something in me. When I worked at Next Retail, I quickly became more than just staff. I wasn’t just folding shirts or checking stock—I became the guy people gravitated toward. Customers would follow my lead, take my advice, and I often found myself walking the floor just speaking to people. My presence sold more than the products did.

That same presence followed me into recruitment—most notably with the British Nursing Association. I became head of recruitment, coordinating shifts for NHS nurses across Kent. But again, it was my energy, not the job title, that made the difference. I was invited into hospitals, met directly with staff, and built genuine relationships. Nurses took on extra shifts simply because I was the one asking. That experience shaped my understanding of connection, loyalty, and service.

But I always knew there was more.

I didn’t leave employment—I evolved into alignment. Today, I work at Distressed Property Group (DPG), a company I’m proud to call home. I’m not a business partner. I don’t own the company. But I run it like it’s mine—because my mentor, who introduced me to this space in 2010, believed in me enough to give me that responsibility.

He trusts me to lead from the front—to manage our clients, oversee our project managers, make strategic decisions, and build this masterpiece we’re co-creating. He’s said it himself: no one outside the legal ownership cares more about this company than I do. And that’s the level of respect I’ve earned—not just as a professional, but as an entrepreneur in the purest sense.

I might be a company man for DPG, but I’m a free thinker. ThinkFree allows me the freedom to express myself fully, and that’s rare. Rare to be able to operate within a structure and still have full creative, strategic and emotional investment in what you’re building.

Everywhere I’ve worked—from retail to recruitment to property—I’ve been seen as one of the best, if not the best. Not because I chased the title, but because I showed up with passion, commitment, and consistency. That’s what entrepreneurship means to me. It’s not always about ownership—it’s about how you show up. It’s about the care you bring into what you do.

And if you truly care about something, you’ll naturally build it like it’s your own.

Wealth isn’t just about money. It’s about meaning. And I bring that into every deal, every day.
